radiology_report:
Tergooi MC
Department of Radiology
Date: 12 Feb 2025
Exam: mpMRI prostate

Clinical indication: Re-evaluation of known prostate cancer. PSA 4.8 ng/mL.

FINDINGS:
The prostate gland is enlarged with a total volume of 90.82 mL. The peripheral zone demonstrates heterogeneous signal intensity. In the right base of the peripheral zone, a focal lesion measuring approximately 12 x 10 mm is identified. On T2-weighted imaging, this lesion appears as a discrete hypointense area. Diffusion-weighted imaging shows restricted diffusion within the lesion, which is confirmed by low signal on the ADC map. Dynamic contrast-enhanced sequences demonstrate early and intense enhancement of the lesion compared to the surrounding tissue. The central gland shows benign prostatic hyperplasia nodules without suspicious focal lesions. No extracapsular extension or seminal vesicle invasion is visualized. No pelvic lymphadenopathy is seen.

IMPRESSION:
Focal lesion in the right base of the peripheral zone, consistent with PI-RADS 4.
Prostate volume 90.82 mL, PSA density 0.053 ng/mL/mL.
Clinical T stage cT1c.
csPCa predicted probability 0.46945655.

previous_notes.author: Dr. S. de Vries (GP)
previous_notes.text: Patient presented with a PSA of 3.8 ng/mL, showing a steady rise from 2.9 ng/mL in October 2023. A transrectal ultrasound-guided prostate biopsy was performed, which confirmed adenocarcinoma, Gleason 3+3, ISUP grade group 1. The patient was informed of the diagnosis and the options for active surveillance versus treatment. He expressed a preference for active surveillance, given the low-risk nature of the disease. Follow-up was scheduled for October 2024.

previous_notes.author: Dr. S. de Vries (GP)
previous_notes.text: Patient returned for follow-up. PSA had increased to 4.8 ng/mL. He reported no new urinary symptoms and continued to feel well. He mentioned recent appointments for varicose veins and cataract review, which are unrelated to his prostate condition. He was referred to urology for re-evaluation of his prostate cancer diagnosis and to discuss further management options.

Specimen: Transrectal ultrasound-guided prostate biopsy, 2022

Histological examination of the prostate tissue samples reveals adenocarcinoma. The Gleason score is 3+3, corresponding to ISUP grade group 1. No cribriform or intraductal patterns are identified. Perineural invasion is not observed. The tumour is located in the peripheral zone, base right.
